analysis.title: Nomura Cross-Asset: FLOWING, 30 October 2026
key_insights: AI capex, free cash flow and financing sustainability concerns are back at the forefront after several MegaCap Tech and Hyperscaler earnings showed weakening trends in core businesses versus high expectations. The FCF implications raise doubts about the durability of the capex trickle-down story and the funding needed for the mega capex projections, with more debt and equity issuance supply expected.

McElligott sees the equity move as mainly positioning excess and a gross leverage and risk-management exercise into year-end. Leveraged investors are worried about drawdown timing ahead of comp and bonus season and about capital being reduced before the new year's PNL turn, so tolerance for losses is low and there is little incentive to deploy risk on mean reversion.

Index options skew has not reacted much to the few days of spot equity selloff this week. Call vol has been compressed week-to-date. Nasdaq vol is outperforming spot today but is still lower than a week ago because earnings events have cleared.

SPX OTM puts are not being chased for three reasons: high dispersion keeps correlation low (9 S&P sectors higher WTD and MTD against a mainly Mag7 downdraft, with only 2 sectors down), de-grossing feeds dispersion (shorts covered higher, longs sold lower) and keeps index vol subdued, and with lower exposure and fewer high nets there is less need to pay for downside hedges. The selling is concentrated in AI MegaCap Tech and Hyperscaler names after 1-2 years of large runs.

McElligott is surprised that the renewed wobble in the AI capex trickle-down thesis, which adds some probability to an economic left-tail scenario for 2027/28 and supports the correlation shift where bonds work as an equity hedge, is not pushing USTs higher. The initial impulsive squeeze of crowded CTA trend shorts in bonds and STIRS is now seeing receivers and calls being closed out in vol space.

A further bond rally could trigger negative convexity and gamma acceleration flows, which leaves a 'Spot Up / Vol Up' catalyst for large moves. Rates trades may also be subject to PNL management and profit-taking on tactical longs ('singles and doubles, not homers'), and the CTA model needs 3m windows to turn long from short, which has not happened yet.

Fundamental equity exposure is low, so there is little to de-risk from that group. The risk into the close is mechanical flow from systematic and market-structure forces, probably being front-run into the midday window. This includes real negative gamma (legacy hedges in Nasdaq and single-name tech) and synthetic negative gamma (leveraged ETFs), on top of 95th percentile long equity exposure across systematic funds after suppressed realized vol turned into de-risking supply.

Estimated systematic and dealer flows: vol control de-allocation of about -$31.1B for sale on a -2% SPX move and -$67.2B on -3%. Leveraged ETF implied end-of-day rebalancing is -$35B for sale (0th percentile, 3rd largest ever) because 87% of AUM is tech concentrated. Including options dealer short gamma in index and key singles, a -2% SPX close projects about -$110B for sale in aggregate.

sector_views.rationale: Names are giving back chunks after 1-2 years of large runs, with weakening core business trends, FCF concerns tied to AI capex and heavy debt and equity issuance supply.
